# Numerical inference fixtures

`procedural.png` is an original seeded textured RGB pattern with dark paths,
generated by `tests/generate-parity.py`. It is not a construction inspection
dataset and establishes no detection accuracy, safety or performance result.

`reference.json` records raw-input/model SHA-256 identities and Python package
versions. Gzip files preserve complete unquantized float32 ONNX outputs and the
exact OpenCV input tensors. Together they occupy approximately 8 MB and are test
assets only, not Android/browser application assets.

Run `node --experimental-strip-types tests/inference-parity.mjs` for model
integrity, preprocessing and decoder parity. Add `--wasm` to execute all four real
models using the installed ONNX Runtime Web WASM backend, then repeat inference
with JavaScript-preprocessed input. No extra native runtime package is needed.

The fast decoder check requires identical boxes/classes/counts and mask IoU at
least 0.999 against Python outputs. OpenCV and JavaScript uint8 resize can differ
by one intensity level; the test reports every affected fraction and bounds mean
error to 0.15 intensity levels. Full WASM checks separately report raw runtime
drift and full-pipeline boxes/masks. The latter permits one output-grid cell of
box drift, 0.01 score drift, and mask pixel disagreements up to two output-cell
footprints or 5% of mask union on this input; raw IoU remains visible because
a one-pixel change has a large IoU effect on a tiny component. These tolerances
are numerical regression guards, not field-quality criteria.

Regenerate using the original project's Python environment from the app folder:

```powershell
..\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tests/generate-parity.py
```
